disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.bobcat_otter_permits: Bobcat: Bobcat Hunting and Trapping Permit required BEFORE attempting to harvest (lottery, $5 non-refundable application, applications Sept 1-30 online only); one bobcat per permit; Bobcat Registration Permit ($5) must be purchased within 48 hours of harvest (online only, not at vendors); federal CITES tag mailed 2-3 weeks later. River otter: River Otter Registration Permit ($5) within 48 hours of taking EACH otter; CITES pelt tag mailed 2-3 weeks later.
license_summary.hunting_license: To HUNT furbearers, residents and nonresidents need an applicable hunting license plus a State Habitat Stamp ($5).
license_summary.trapping_license: Residents and nonresidents need an appropriate trapping license plus a State Habitat Stamp ($5) to trap furbearers. First-time trappers born on or after Jan. 1, 1998 must complete a trapper education course before purchasing a license. Youth Hunting and Trapping license (under 18): $7. Nonresident trapping: $175 (with state reciprocity) / $250 (without).

permit_requirements: Bobcat Hunting and Trapping Permit required BEFORE taking or attempting to harvest a bobcat; allocated by lottery; $5 non-refundable application fee; applications online only Sept 1-30.

Bobcat Registration Permit must be purchased online within 48 hours of harvest ($5); NOT available at license vendors. Federal CITES tag mailed 2-3 weeks later and must be permanently affixed to the pelt before export or transfer to a fur buyer, taxidermist, fur tanner, or garment manufacturer.
Applicants who did not receive a permit the previous year get preference in the initial random drawing.

species.iac_reference: 17 Ill. Adm. Code 590; 2026–27 IL Hunt & Trap Digest p.42, 45
species.notes: Licensed trappers may salvage a road-kill river otter during the open season; it counts toward the 5-otter harvest limit and is subject to permit/tagging requirements.
permit_requirements: River Otter Registration Permit ($5) must be purchased within 48 hours of harvesting EACH river otter; available online and at vendors. Do not purchase before harvest.

Official CITES pelt tag mailed 2-3 weeks after purchase; must be permanently affixed to the green hide of each otter (including whole, unskinned carcass) before it is exported from the U.S. or transferred to a fur buyer, fur tanner, taxidermist, or manufacturer. Tags cannot be transferred between people.
Possession limits do not apply to fur buyers, tanners, manufacturers, taxidermists, or to tanned pelts, mounted specimens, or manufactured products.

verification.confirmation_notes: Data taken from the official Illinois DNR 2026-2027 Digest of Hunting and Trapping Regulations (PDF hosted on huntillinois.org, uploaded Aug 2026). Furbearer trapping table and furbearer hunting table both on digest p.42; bobcat/otter permit rules pp.43-45; furbearer and bobcat zone maps p.44. Table images were visually verified against the PDF to resolve ambiguous text-extraction row alignment.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the Illinois DNR digest.
Trapping opening-day time is not stated in the digest; season entries use open_time null.

Bobcat trapping dates: the trapping table merges the date cell across the general-season rows including bobcat (10 Nov 2026 - 15 Feb 2027); confirmed by the digest's 2026-2027 trapping timeline ('Badger/Bobcat/Coyote/... Opens 10').

Bobcat closed zone is described geographically (bounded by I-39/U.S. Route 51 west, U.S. Route 36 south) rather than by county list; modeled as a descriptive special_areas zone. Badger North/South zones are divided by U.S. Route 36, likewise descriptive.

Bobcat hunting hours: the digest merges bobcat's hours cell with the raccoon/opossum/red fox row ('Open 24 hours...'); the merged cell mentions other species explicitly for the archery-deer-season exception but not bobcat — flag for cross-check against 17 Ill. Adm. Code 590 if precise hours matter.

Woodchuck trapping season in the 2026-27 digest (1 Jun - 30 Sep 2026) is already closed as of dataset compilation; the next occurrence (1 Jun - 30 Sep 2027) is an annual-pattern expectation, not a published date.
First and second firearm deer season dates (which close some furbearer hunting) are not modeled.
Depredation/nuisance take (Nuisance Animal Removal Permit) is noted in the digest but not modeled as a season.
Trap hardware rules (snare specs, jaw spread limits, setbacks, tagging, check times) are NOT in this dataset.
